heroSub: Seven budget stays in Sukhothai we've reviewed in depth, all scoring 8.3+ — from an Old Town garden bungalow scoring 9.6 that you can cycle to the ruins from, to the most-reviewed guesthouse by the Yom River, the cheapest wooden garden house at ฿500, and value boutiques with a pool in the New Town. Starting from around ฿500–1,200/night.
introH2: 🏛️ Can you really do Sukhothai on a budget, and which area is best value?
introHtml: Sukhothai is a World Heritage city that's kinder on the wallet than many travellers expect — most stays are guesthouses, garden bungalows and small boutiques with strong guest scores in the low-hundreds-to-just-over-a-thousand baht range, and a clean, comfortable ฿500–1,000 night is easy to find. The key to doing Sukhothai on a budget is matching the area to your trip, because the city splits into two zones that feel and cost distinctly different. The Old Town is the zone around the Historical Park — stays here are garden resorts and bungalows, you can cycle to the ancient ruins straight from your hotel, and it's quiet but with few dinner options at night. The New Town sits about 12 km away by the Yom River — a district of value guesthouses, walkable to markets, restaurants and the songthaew stop into the park. This guide brings together 7 budget stays in Sukhothai we've reviewed in depth, all scoring 8.3+ — every pick comes from reading real guest reviews, gives the honest ups and downs, compares prices across 3 sites and links direct throughout. We list 7 honestly, because we only include stays that are genuinely budget and good value — no padding the list to ten with pricier resorts.
mrtHtml: Sukhothai has no metro and the city is compact — you'll mostly use cars, motorbikes, bicycles or songthaews. From Sukhothai Airport into the Old Town is about 40 minutes. The areas in this guide: Old Town — around the Sukhothai Historical Park, Wat Mahathat, Wat Si Chum; most stays lend free bicycles so you can cycle to the ruins from your door (Thai Thai, Phiphu) · New Town — by the Yom River, near markets and restaurants, value guesthouses and boutiques, about 15–20 minutes by songthaew to the park (TR Guesthouse, At Home, Baan Georges, Ban Thai, Aen Guy) · If your trip is mainly about the ruins, the Old Town gets you into the park more directly. If you want convenience for food and the lowest prices, choose the New Town · Most stays in both areas either provide bikes or help arrange transport to the park.

entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old Town · cycle to the Historical Park
entries.addr: Chedi Thong Rd, Mueang Kao, Mueang Sukhothai
entries.storyHtml: The top-scoring stay in this guide starts at just around ฿900/night yet scores 9.6 from 211 reviews — Thai Thai Sukhothai Resort is a garden-bungalow resort in the Old Town that guests love for both the staff and the atmosphere. Reviewers consistently praise the friendly, helpful staff, the generous fresh breakfast, and the pool to cool off in after a day at the ruins; it's an easy cycle to the Historical Park from your door. The honest caveats: some in-building rooms are smaller than the bungalows so check the type, it's on a quiet lane where places nearby close early, and the garden gets a few mosquitoes at times. Best for travellers here mainly for the ruins who want a value garden bungalow in the Old Town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a Superior Double Bungalow for a garden-view balcony and more space, as some in-building rooms are smaller. Bring mosquito repellent for the garden, and pack late-night snacks since the lane is quiet and shops close early.

entries.addr: 27/5 Pravet Nakorn Rd, Mueang Sukhothai (New Town)
entries.storyHtml: If you want a proven budget guesthouse, TR Guesthouse is the most-reviewed stay in this guide — over 520 reviews, scoring 8.8, from just ฿600/night. The strength is its central New Town location, walkable to restaurants and the market, with friendly hosts who arrange transport and motorbike rentals. There are both air-conditioned in-building rooms and quieter, more private garden bungalows; rooms are clean with comfortable beds. The honest caveats: facilities are simple with no pool or gym, and breakfast isn't included in every rate (it can be added). Best for backpackers and budget couples who want to be in the New Town, walkable to food, with hosts who help plan the trip.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pick a Garden Bungalow for privacy and a garden-view balcony, and rent a motorbike here to ride out to the Old Town yourself — cheaper than chartering a car. Ask about breakfast when you book, as some rates don't include it.

entries.type: Boutique B&B 3-Star · art house · Old Town
entries.name: Phiphu Art and Gallery Boutique
entries.revCount: Score 9.0 · 120 reviews · Old Town boutique B&B, walk to the park
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Old Town · 15-min walk to the Historical Park
entries.storyHtml: To stay in the Old Town within walking distance of the park for under a thousand baht, Phiphu Art and Gallery Boutique earns a high 9.0 guest score from 120 reviews, from just ฿950/night. The rooms are spacious and clean with a big fridge and a roomy bathroom, decorated with artwork so it feels like staying at a local's home; it's a 15-minute walk to the Historical Park, with free bikes to borrow and free parking, and warm hosts. The honest caveats: staff speak limited English so a translation app helps, and as a small B&B there's no pool or full facilities. Best for travellers here mainly for the ruins who want a value stay in the Old Town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ideal if the ruins are your main focus — borrow a free bike for an early-morning ride before it gets hot. Have a translation app handy, and if there are four of you, the Classic Quadruple splits down cheaper per head.

entries.addr: 184/1 Wichian Chamnong Rd, Mueang Sukhothai (New Town)
entries.storyHtml: The cheapest stay in this guide starts at just ฿500, but with the charm of a wooden house in a garden — At Home Sukhothai scores 8.8 from 213 reviews. The draw is a generous, tasty breakfast served in the garden by a lotus pond, with lounge corners and hammocks to relax in, plus hosts who arrange transport and recommend places to visit; there are fan rooms, air-con rooms and garden bungalows. The honest caveats: it's a wooden garden house so some rooms get mosquitoes (bring repellent), and it's about 10–12 km from the Historical Park, needing a songthaew or rental. Best for backpackers and budget couples who want atmosphere over a generic in-building guesthouse.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose an Air-Con Room or higher in the hot season, as the fan rooms get warm. Bring mosquito repellent, and sort a motorbike or ask the hosts about the songthaew into the park on day one.

entries.storyHtml: For a boutique with a pool in the New Town without paying resort prices, Baan Georges Hotel is a tiny 8-room boutique pool hotel with a warm, stay-with-a-friend feel, scoring 8.7 from 263 reviews, from ฿1,200/night. The standout many reviews mention is the rooftop breakfast with fresh-baked bread and brewed coffee, plus hosts who welcome you like family; there's a pool to cool off in — rare at this price — and it's a few minutes' walk to restaurants and street food in the New Town. The honest caveats: the entrance is down a deep lane with several soi dogs that bark at night, and it's about 15 minutes by car from the park. Best for couples who want a boutique with a pool and a good breakfast in the low-thousands, in the New Town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With only 8 rooms it fills fast in high season, so book ahead. Watch out for the soi dogs if you're walking back late, and don't miss the rooftop breakfast — it's the highlight in many reviews.

entries.storyHtml: A family guesthouse travellers have talked about for years on Pravet Nakorn Road — Ban Thai Guesthouse scores 8.4 from 256 reviews, from ฿550/night. What really stands out is the owners' warm welcome, like staying at a relative's home, and the on-site restaurant that reviews praise for taste and value; you can pick an air-con in-building room or a bungalow in the garden with a fish pond and shady trees, a few minutes' walk from the night market and songthaew stop. The honest caveats: the fan bungalows get hot in the hot season and some have no mosquito net, and some rooms are small with no pool. Best for backpackers and budget couples who want a family garden atmosphere and easy walking to food.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: In the hot season or if you dislike mosquitoes, choose an air-con bungalow — cooler, with a garden and fish-pond view. Don't miss dinner at the on-site restaurant in the garden, and tell the hosts ahead if you'd like help with transport or a bike to the park.

entries.storyHtml: Rounding out the guide is a boutique that gives you a pool and an on-site café in the low-thousands — Aen Guy Boutique Hotel is a roughly 35-room 3-star boutique in the New Town, on the main Jarodvithithong Road, scoring 8.3 from 216 reviews, from ฿1,000/night. What sets it apart from similarly priced stays is an outdoor pool (with a kids' pool) and the on-site Aen Guy Coffee café open 08:00–21:00, plus free parking right on the main road for easy in-and-out. The honest caveats: road-facing rooms can hear traffic during the day so ask for an inner or pool-side room, breakfast options are limited, and it's about 20 minutes by car from the Historical Park. Best for those driving themselves who want a boutique with a pool and café and an easy-access New Town location.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for an inner or pool-side room when you book, as road-facing rooms can hear traffic. Make the most of the on-site café for your first coffee, and if you're driving, the free parking right on the main road is a real plus here.

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about budget hotels in Sukhothai

faq.q: ❓ Which budget hotel in Sukhothai is the best value?
faq.a: On score-per-baht, Thai Thai Sukhothai Resort at 9.6 from ฿900 is the top-scoring stay in this guide, and you can cycle to the park from it. On the lowest budget, At Home Sukhothai from ฿500 is the cheapest wooden garden house, scoring 8.8, while Ban Thai Guesthouse at ฿550 and TR Guesthouse at ฿600 (the most reviewed, 520 reviews) are proven value in the New Town.

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget hotels in Sukhothai cost?
faq.a: In this guide, indicative starting rates are ฿500–1,200 a night. The lightest are At Home from ฿500, Ban Thai ฿550 and TR Guesthouse ฿600; the bungalow/boutique end is Thai Thai ฿900, Phiphu ฿950, Aen Guy ฿1,000 and Baan Georges ฿1,200. All are indicative starting rates from standard rooms; during the Loy Krathong festival (Nov) they can run higher and fill fast.

faq.q: ❓ On a budget, should I stay in the Old Town or New Town?
faq.a: It depends on your trip. The Old Town suits ruins-focused trips — stays are garden bungalows and you can cycle to the ruins from your door (Thai Thai, Phiphu), but there are few dinner options at night. The New Town, about 12 km away by the Yom River, is walkable to markets and restaurants with the lowest-priced stays (TR Guesthouse, At Home, Ban Thai, Baan Georges, Aen Guy), 15–20 minutes by songthaew to the park.

faq.q: ❓ Are there budget stays in Sukhothai you can cycle to the park from?
faq.a: Yes — the Old Town stays in this guide are easy to cycle to the Historical Park from. Thai Thai Sukhothai Resort (฿900) is a cycle to the park from your door, and Phiphu Art and Gallery (฿950) is a 15-minute walk with free bikes to borrow. The New Town stays need a songthaew or rented motorbike into the park, about 15–20 minutes.

faq.q: ❓ Are there budget stays in Sukhothai with a swimming pool?
faq.a: Several in this guide. Baan Georges Hotel (฿1,200) is a tiny 8-room boutique with a pool and a rooftop breakfast; Aen Guy Boutique Hotel (฿1,000) has a pool and kids' pool plus an on-site café; and Thai Thai Sukhothai Resort (฿900) is a garden bungalow with a pool. The cheapest guesthouses — At Home, Ban Thai and TR Guesthouse — have no pool.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a budget hotel in Sukhothai?
faq.a: For normal weekdays, 1–2 weeks ahead is enough. But during the Loy Krathong / Light & Candle Festival (November), Sukhothai's biggest event, rooms fill very fast — especially small stays like Baan Georges (8 rooms) — so book 1–2 months ahead. All platforms offer Free Cancellation, so lock a rate early if plans aren't firm, then compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.
